# Hermes Agent: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

---

### 1. Installation & Platform Support

**Q: Can I run Hermes Agent natively on Windows?**  
Yes. Windows 10/11 is a Tier 1 supported platform via the native PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`). WSL2 is not required for core CLI/agent features, though WSL2 is recommended if you need the embedded terminal pane in the web dashboard (which requires a POSIX PTY).

**Q: Is ARM64 (e.g., Raspberry Pi 4B, Apple Silicon) supported?**  
Yes. `scripts/install.sh` automatically detects `aarch64`, `arm64`, and `armv7l` architectures and handles Node/Python dependencies without special configuration.

**Q: Is there a Web UI, or is Hermes CLI-only?**  
Hermes includes a first-party web dashboard. Run `hermes dashboard` to start the local server and open `http://127.0.0.1:9119` in your browser. It includes a browser-based **Chat** interface embedding the full TUI.

**Q: Why does `hermes update` hang on "Updating Node.js dependencies"?**  
This is expected behavior during the Camofox post-install step, which silently downloads browser binaries in the background without a progress bar. Let it finish.

---

### 2. Model Configuration & Providers

**Q: How do I use my Claude Pro / Max subscription instead of paying API token fees?**  
Using an Anthropic API key always bills via standard pay-as-you-go API usage. To use your Claude Pro/Max subscription allowance, you must authenticate using **OAuth**, not an API key.

**Q: How do I configure Microsoft Azure AI Foundry or Azure OpenAI?**  
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` (it auto-detects `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`) or set `provider: azure-foundry`. Note: Claude Code-specific env vars (e.g., `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`) are not used.
- **Azure OpenAI:** Custom base URLs with query parameters (e.g., `https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai?api-version=2025-04-01-preview`) are supported; `api-version` parameters are automatically preserved.

**Q: How do I connect to Google Gemini?**  
Legacy CLI OAuth (`google-gemini-cli` / `google-antigravity`) is deprecated. Use Google AI Studio with `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` or configure Vertex AI.

---

### 3. Autonomy, Goals & Sessions

**Q: What is the tool-call limit, and how do I run long autonomous tasks?**  
- By default, single turns cap at `agent.max_turns` (default: 90) to prevent infinite loops. You can override this per run using `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`.
- For persistent, multi-turn autonomous execution, use the `/goal` command. Goals persist across turn budgets; if paused when the iteration limit is reached, run `/goal resume` to continue.

**Q: Why did my chat session reset in Telegram or messaging gateways?**  
Interrupted or crashed sessions are placed in `resume_pending` status and can be restored with `/resume`. Automatic idle resets are disabled by default (`session_reset.mode: none` in `config.yaml`).

**Q: Can messaging bots (e.g., Discord) read uploaded code and text files?**  
Yes. Text-readable attachments (such as `.py`, `.txt`, and code files) uploaded in authorized Discord/gateway channels are cached and automatically injected into the prompt.

---

### 4. Multi-Agent, Personas & Isolation

**Q: How do subagents and multi-agent coordination work?**  
Hermes provides the `delegate_task` tool, which spawns isolated child `AIAgent` instances with their own contexts and toolsets. It supports single-task and parallel batch modes (default: up to 3 concurrent subagents).

**Q: Can I set different personas for different chat channels?**  
Yes. Use the `channel_prompts` configuration in your platform settings (supported on Discord, Telegram, Slack, and Mattermost) to map channel/group IDs to distinct system prompts. Dynamic routing is also possible via `pre_llm_call` plugin hooks.

**Q: How do I run multiple isolated agents without shared state or file collisions?**  
- **Profiles (Recommended):** Run `hermes profile create <name>` and `hermes profile use <name>` (or pass `--profile <name>` / set `HERMES_PROFILE=<name>`). Each profile has its own `config.yaml`, `SOUL.md`, memories, skills, and credentials. Multiple profiles can be served simultaneously via gateway multiplexing.
- **Separate Homes:** Set `HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes-<name>` to isolate entire directory trees.

---

### 5. Memory, Soul & Custom Tools

**Q: What is the difference between `SOUL.md`, `USER.md`, and `MEMORY.md`?**  
- `SOUL.md`: Defines the agent's identity, system prompt, backstory, and core persona.
- `USER.md`: Stores persistent profile details, identity, and preferences about *you* (updated via memory tool `target="user"`).
- `MEMORY.md`: General persistent working memory and notes across interactions.

**Q: How do I add custom tools?**  
Create a plugin under `~/.hermes/plugins/`, register tools using `ctx.register_tool(...)`, and enable it with `hermes plugins enable <name>`. For built-in development in the core repo, add tools to `tools/*.py` and register them in `toolsets.py`.
